sections.html:
Georgetown County stretches from the Atlantic shore inland along several rivers, and roughly a fifth of it is water. The county measures 1,034.83 square miles overall, with 813.61 of land, and counted 63,404 residents in 2020. The city of Georgetown holds the county seat, while Murrells Inlet is the most populous community. Pawleys Island, DeBordieu, Litchfield Beach, Plantersville, North Santee and Andrews are also on the map. Andrews lies partly in Williamsburg County, and Garden City sits mostly in Horry County.

Hotels and restaurants, health care and retail supply the most jobs. Heritage tourism and retirement living have grown lately, which influences who shops for coastal homes.

Few parcels here are far from water. Four rivers, the Great Pee Dee, Waccamaw, Black and Sampit, empty into Winyah Bay, the Santee River marks the southern edge and the Intracoastal Waterway cuts across. Georgetown city stands about 3 feet above sea level. Hurricane Hugo brought wind and surge up the rivers in September 1989, and Hurricane Ian made landfall near Georgetown in September 2022. Rain at Georgetown County Airport averages about 55.43 inches a year, heaviest from June through September.

  • Request the parcel's flood zone and elevation record ahead of listing.
  • Collect any roof, window and wind-damage repair records.
  • Make sure the stormwater fee is paid, because it rides along on the tax bill.

With those answers in hand, a buyer's questions about storm history are easy to meet.

Payment season is fixed by the state, running from September 30 to January 15, and after that the penalties begin. Section 12-45-180 puts 3 percent on after January 15, 7 percent more after February 1 and 5 percent more after March 16, totaling 15 percent.

Your bill carries the exact dates. Notices and collections are the Treasurer's job, and the money is then distributed to the county, towns, schools and special districts. The Treasurer does not set amounts: value comes from the Assessor and the tax figure from the Auditor.

The stormwater fee is printed on the property tax bill and falls due the same day. If you think it is wrong, appeal in writing to the director of Public Services within 30 days of the decision, enclosing a map that shows total area and impervious surface. Fees left unpaid can become liens.

sections.h2: Tax offices and how to reach them
sections.html:
County government is at 129 Screven Street, Georgetown, SC 29442. Write to P.O. Box 421270, Georgetown, SC 29442-4200, or call the main number, 843-545-3063.

The county's tax services page links separate pages for the Assessor, Auditor, Treasurer, Tax Collector, the Tax Sale and Forfeited Land Commission, and appeals. The offices depend on taxpayers to report new addresses, so a seller who has moved should tell both the Assessor and the Auditor.

Every five years the state calls for a countywide reassessment, and Georgetown's latest was in 2025, with notices mailed September 15, 2025. A notice went only to properties whose value moved by $1,000 or more, and it is not a tax bill. Bills follow later in the fall.

Most long-held properties are capped at a 15 percent rise over the prior value. Exceptions include homes sold or transferred in the previous year, new construction or additions and newly added parcels. A capped property shows two values on its notice. A millage rollback is also mandatory, so reassessment cannot bring the county extra revenue. The county says the effect on taxpayers overall is little to none, although an individual bill can change.

  • Primary residence: ask the Assessor for the 4 percent rate.
  • Homestead exemption: owners 65 or older may apply to the Auditor to exempt up to $50,000 of value.
  • ATI exemption: buyers of rentals or commercial property may ask the Auditor to cut the assessed value increase caused by a change of ownership by up to 25 percent.

sections.h2: How to appeal a Georgetown County value
sections.html:
A written objection is due within 90 days of the notice date. An informal appeal form comes with the notice, and an appraiser in the Assessor's Office reviews it. You do not need to hire an appraiser, filing is free and you may attach recent appraisals or sales data.

Still unhappy? Request a hearing at the Board of Assessment Appeals, and after that the South Carolina Administrative Law Court. An appeal does not hold up the tax bill, so pay on time and avoid penalties.

This year's annual sale falls on Monday, December 7, 2026, in County Council Chambers, 129 Screven Street. Advance registration costs $25 and closes at noon on Friday, December 4. Bidding opens at 10:00 a.m., and winners pay in full by 5:00 p.m. the same day.

The Coastal Observer carries three consecutive weeks of advertising for the properties. Redemption within 12 months is open to the owner, a grantee, or a mortgage or judgment creditor. Interest is 3 percent in months one to three, 6 percent in months four to six, 9 percent in months seven to nine and 12 percent in the last three months, never above the forfeited land commission's bid. A tax deed is not a warranty deed, and the county tells buyers to talk to an attorney.

Georgetown sellers can save time by gathering a few records. Start with the latest tax bill, which shows the stormwater fee and whether the 4 percent rate is in place. Add the 2025 reassessment notice, since it shows the capped and uncapped values and tells a buyer what to expect. If you own a rental or commercial property and just bought it, ask the Auditor about the ATI exemption.

Then deal with the physical side of a coastal house. Buyers ask about flood zones, roof age and storm repairs, so a folder with those records speeds up the conversation. Offices rely on you to report address changes, so confirm that the Assessor and the Auditor both have the right mailing address before closing.

sections.h2: Selling a Georgetown County house with taxes due
sections.html:
If your parcel could be on the sale list, ask the Delinquent Tax Department what is owed today. A seller with a balance can generally still close, and the title company pays the taxes, penalties and any stormwater fee from the proceeds.

  1. Ask for the amount owed and the date it holds through.
  2. Check your 4 percent rate or exemption status with the Assessor or Auditor.
  3. Pull flood zone and elevation records.
  4. Give the Assessor and Auditor your current mailing address.

faqs.q: When are Georgetown County property taxes due?
faqs.a: January 15, under state law. Penalties then begin at 3 percent, add 7 percent after February 1 and add 5 percent after March 16.

faqs.q: Does Georgetown County have a stormwater fee on the tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes, it appears as a line on the property tax bill, with the same due date as the taxes.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Georgetown County property value?
faqs.a: Ninety days from the notice date. Use the form that arrives with the notice, and the Assessor's Office reviews it at no cost.

faqs.q: When is the Georgetown County tax sale in 2026?
faqs.a: It is on Monday, December 7, 2026, with bidding at 10:00 a.m. in County Council Chambers at 129 Screven Street. Sign up by noon on December 4.

faqs.q: Does a Georgetown County reassessment mean my taxes go up?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. The county rolls the millage back when values rise, so some bills go up, some fall, and the total collected stays about the same.
